title: Chapter 24
content:
Sticking an unlit cigarette between his lips, Jakyeong stared at his reflection in the bathroom mirror, completely at a loss for words.

Two full days had passed, yet the angry crimson marks blooming across his chest were as vivid as ever. The bastard had sucked and chewed on his nipples with such relentless ferocity that they even looked slightly swollen. Was he starved of maternal affection as an infant, or what? The man possessed a borderline psychotic fixation on his chest.

Jakyeong brushed a thumb over the tender bud—a sharp, electric sting flared instantly, wrenching a foul curse from his throat.

"Of all the insane things I've done in this life... getting handled like that by a fucking man."

And was that all? Far from it. Even if he could excuse how it started as a reluctant transaction, by the end, he had been panting right alongside the bastard, rocking his hips and wrapping his legs around Kang Il-hyun’s waist like a willing partner.

Locating the target asset in the safe should have lifted a massive weight off his chest, but every time the visceral memory of that night crept up, his stomach twisted into knots.

Fortunately, Il-hyun had been swamped with business and hadn't shown his face for the past two days. It was a massive relief. Jakyeong had already transmitted photos of the flash drive to Wang Han's team to source an identical dummy unit; once that was secured, he could breathe easy. Until then, his only prayer was to avoid getting tangled up with that lunatic's body ever again.

Stepping out into the bedroom, a wall of stifling, humid air hit him square in the face.

The air conditioning had completely cut out. Apparently, one of the heavy construction trucks working on the pool had backed into a utility pole down the road, taking down the estate's power grid.

Heading down to the ground floor, Jakyeong walked over to the floor-to-ceiling windows. Outside, laborers were bustling across the lawn in the heat.

The glass pane was brand new, bearing zero traces of the sniper round that had punched through it days ago. The bullet recovered from the wall had been a .338 Lapua Magnum—a high-velocity, match-grade round favored by elite marksmen for its flat trajectory and terrifying kinetic punch. That morning had been dead calm, clear skies with zero crosswind—textbook conditions for a clean headshot.

Yet the round hadn't targeted Jakyeong’s heart. It had sliced toward his right shoulder.

It wasn't a miss. The shooter’s objective was almost certainly to wound and incapacitate Jang Yi-an. As the sole grandson of Jang Myeong—the venerable Triad patriarch allied with Haewon Group—an injury to Yi-an on Korean soil would place Kang Il-hyun in an impossible, politically lethal bind.

Who ordered the hit?

The faces of the family members gathered at the patriarch's dinner table flashed through his mind one by one.

"Yi-an!"

A familiar, grating voice shattered his train of thought. Turning around, Jakyeong saw Kang Seok-joo waving an arm as he sauntered into the living room. He’d called earlier that morning, and upon hearing that Jakyeong was under house arrest, he had driven straight over.

"Is this the spot? Wow, not even a scratch left on the glass, huh?" Seok-joo grinned, leaning in to inspect the pristine pane.

Jakyeong easily read the subtext behind the visit. "You look thrilled."

"Thrilled? Nah, disappointed is more like it." Seok-joo glanced over his shoulder to ensure the room was clear, then dropped his voice to a malicious whisper. "The bullet should've gone through Executive Director Kang's skull."

Jakyeong offered a thin smile. The fact that the kid dropped treasonous remarks so casually showed just how comfortable he felt around him. Seok-joo seemed far more animated here than he had at the family dinner. Then again, surviving in a pit full of hyenas would drain the life out of anyone.

Jakyeong signaled a maid to bring up a tray of iced tea, then led Seok-joo up to the second-floor lounge. Sinking into the sofa, he steered the conversation with casual indifference toward Choi Ki-tae.

"Ki-tae? That psycho's running around like a headless chicken right now," Seok-joo scoffed.

"Why? What happened?"

Seok-joo kicked his feet up onto the coffee table, crossing his ankles with smug arrogance. "Well, his old man runs a pharmaceutical racket. You know, 'gear.' The stuff we were doing the other night."

"Right."

"Turns out someone hijacked their crew. The work mules."

"Mules? Who did it?"

"Hell if I know. The kids were all underage, and whoever snatched them had the bright idea to dump them right on the doorstep of the local police precinct before vanishing into thin air. But the cops turned around and called Ki-tae’s old man to come collect them."

Jakyeong’s posture froze. His jaw clamped tight, a cold, lethal fury igniting behind his irises.

"They're minors..." Jakyeong murmured, keeping his voice eerily level. "The police didn't transfer them to child protective services?"

"Look at you, so innocent," Seok-joo snickered. "They're runaway street trash with nowhere to go. Ki-tae's father has hooks buried deep in the precinct brass, so they handed the brats right back. That's why power is everything, man. When you've got the cash and the leverage, the cops roll over like trained dogs."

Seok-joo preened, wearing a swollen, proud smirk as if he were the one sitting at the apex of that corrupt food chain.

Jakyeong sat in suffocating silence. The hollow, desperate eyes of the children he had pulled out of that van burned behind his eyelids.

"So... what happened to them? Are they... back on the street working drops?"

"Are you kidding? Who the fuck trusts runners once they've tried to bolt? They're getting disposed of."

"Disposed of?"

"Don't worry your pretty little head about it," Seok-joo waved it off with a chuckle, refusing to elaborate.

Jakyeong didn't need him to.

He knew the underworld's playbook by heart. When child couriers outlived their usefulness, their organs were harvested for the black market, or they were trafficked into underground brothels for depraved elites. And if all else failed, they were butchered into fertilizer and fed to the hounds—a gruesome fate the scarred thugs who visited his mother used to brag about.

Back then, young Jakyeong had thought it was a sick joke—until he stumbled upon the severed hand of a kid his age rotting in the dog pens behind the shantytown. The paralyzing terror that he might end up as dog feed next had haunted his nightmares for years.

The warmth drained entirely from Jakyeong's eyes.

Should I have driven them somewhere else instead of a police station? Or should I have turned a blind eye from the very beginning? Why the hell did I intervene only to deliver those miserable kids straight into a slaughterhouse?

Fuck.

Jakyeong pushed himself up from the sofa.

"What's up? Where are you going?" Seok-joo blinked.

"Sorry. I've got a splitting headache. I need to lie down and sleep it off."

Seok-joo scrambled to his feet, scowling in annoyance. "Are you serious? What am I supposed to do then?"

"I'm not allowed off the grounds anyway, you know that. I'm really sorry."

Flashing a tight, apologetic smile, Jakyeong slipped into the master bedroom and clicked the door shut. Left standing in the lounge, Seok-joo pouted, muttering a string of bitter curses under his breath—complaining that an international VIP had no right to invite someone over just to ditch them for a nap. He kicked the mahogany table leg in frustration, spun on his heel, and slammed the suite door on his way out.

Inside the bedroom, Jakyeong paced the carpet, dragging heavily on his e-cigarette. Fuming, he scrubbed a rough palm over his face.

Dropping to his knees, he unlocked the floor safe and pulled out a folded architectural schematic: the blueprint detailing every blind spot and CCTV camera across the estate grounds. Committing the angles and patrol sweeps to memory, he stashed the paper back into the vault.

From the safe, he retrieved a compact tactical pen-light, an expandable steel baton, and a set of lock-picks, concealing them within his clothing.

Heading downstairs, he found the senior housekeeper in the kitchen, prepping dinner with two junior maids.

"Young Master Yi-an? Is something the matter?"

"The noise outside is a bit loud. How much longer will the pool crew be working?"

"They're packing up the final equipment right now," she assured him warmly. "The utility company said the main power should be restored shortly."

"I see... There's no emergency generator on the property?"

"Goodness, no. This is the first blackout since the estate was built, so we were all caught off guard."

"Understood... Actually, I'm coming down with a severe fever, so I'll be skipping dinner tonight. I took some medicine and plan to sleep straight through."

"Oh, dear! Shall I prepare a hot broth for you?"

"No, thank you. When I'm sick, uninterrupted rest is the only cure. If Director Kang returns and asks for me, please let him know."

He added a self-deprecating comment that once he fell asleep, a bomb going off wouldn't wake him—a clear, polite instruction not to disturb his room under any circumstances.

Understanding the hint, the housekeeper offered a reassuring smile. "If you need anything at all during the night, just use the house phone."

"Thank you, ma'am."

Bowing politely, Jakyeong retreated upstairs.

Inside the guest suite, he drew the heavy blackout blinds and locked the door. He arranged pillows beneath the duvet to create the convincing silhouette of a sleeping body, then slipped into the master bathroom. With the door shut, the windowless room was plunged into pitch-black darkness.

Flicking on his pen-light, he climbed onto the marble rim of the bathtub and unlatched the exhaust panel. Illuminating the shaft, the clearance was brutally tight. Getting wedged to death inside an air duct before I even reach the street would be a pathetic way to go.

Tossing the pen-light into the duct, he braced his forearms against the frame and hauled his upper body upward.

Dragging his lower half through the intake, he began inching forward. Thick layers of gray dust tickled his nose, threatening a violent sneeze. Clamping his teeth around the pen-light, he held his breath, worming his way through the metal shaft inch by grueling inch. With the summer heat baking the unpowered mansion, the claustrophobic duct felt like a furnace, sweat drenching his clothes in sheets.

Fortunately, past the first ninety-degree bend, the main trunk line opened up significantly. Exhaling a ragged breath, he crawled forward, sweat stinging his eyes.

After several yards, a beam of daylight sliced through the darkness ahead. The large industrial exhaust fan on the exterior wall was dead, frozen by the blackout.

Using his baton as a lever, Jakyeong popped the housing pins, wrenched the heavy louvers aside, and poked his head out into the fresh air.

Drawing a deep, silent lungful of clean oxygen, he surveyed the exterior wall. Positioned directly below the vent were two dome security cameras. Despite the main grid being offline, the subtle hum of battery-backup units meant the lenses were still active.

Fucking typical.

Drawing the collapsed steel rod from his waistband, he pressed the release catch. The baton extended with a muffled snap.

Leaning out, he carefully nudged the casing of the first camera, shifting its optical angle forty-five degrees into the brickwork. He mirrored the motion on the second unit, clearing a blind corridor.

Wriggling the rest of his torso through the vent, he gripped the exterior ledge, lowered himself to full extension, and dropped silently onto the manicured turf below, absorbing the impact in a tight combat roll.

Pressing his spine flat against the foundation, he scanned for an extraction route. This courtyard held the lowest camera density, but rounding the corner meant walking straight into high-definition coverage—and a wall covered in dense, thorny climbing roses.

Jakyeong locked eyes on the perimeter wall ahead, drawing a slow, focused breath. It was high, but manageable.

He broke into a silent sprint, launched himself off the turf, snagged the lip of the concrete wall with his fingertips, and hauled his boots up the sheer surface. A few days of sitting around eating luxury meals, and my reaction time is already rusting.

He cleared the coping and dropped down onto the exterior access road with a muffled thud.

The surrounding woods were quiet, broken only by the distant shouting of utility workers repairing the transformer down the hill.

Hugging the tree line, Jakyeong advanced along the perimeter wall before sliding smoothly beneath the chassis of the construction van parked outside the main gates.

Minutes later, the iron gates creaked open. Several laborers strolled out, chatting casually with the security guards about project timelines and restored power.

The van doors slammed shut. The diesel engine roared to life.

As the construction van accelerated down the private mountain road, Lee Ja-kyeong slipped out into the city without leaving a ghost behind.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • .338 Lapua Magnum (338 라푸아 매그넘탄): A specialized military sniper cartridge designed for extreme long-range anti-personnel precision (effective up to 1,500–1,800 meters). Jakyeong calculating the windage, trajectory, and target placement highlights his professional tactical background.

  • Underworld Child Exploitation (미성년자 폐기처분): A grim staple of gritty Korean noir; when street-level drug runners (jige-kkun) are compromised by police contact, syndicates view them as contaminated assets and dispose of them through black-market organ harvesting or underground trafficking rings to prevent institutional leaks.
